Persistent potassium and sulfur deficiencies likely had a significant impact on yield potential, while moderate weed pressure and unresolved stink bug activity at the critical reproductive window likely had a moderate yield impact.

**Season Detail:**
Stand count was 101% detections in the field of target, indicating strong emergence and establishment.

Weed pressure was mild at VE-V1, escalated to very high at V3-V4, then declined to mild and remained mild through the rest of the season; pigweeds, barnyard grass, and volunteer corn were dominant, with pressure concentrated in localized pockets and favorable moisture following 2.9 in of rain on May 16 likely supporting additional weed germination — likely having a moderate yield impact.

Potassium deficiency was first detected at V6-V12 (0.8% detections in the field), concentrated in about 7% of the field, and was no longer detected by the final mission. Nitrogen deficiency was first detected at V6-V12 (0.4%), peaking at 8.6%, and sulfur deficiency was detected once at V13-V16 (38.5%) — persistent deficiencies likely had a significant yield impact.

Rust was present in up to 1 field regionally but was not detected in this field — likely negligible yield impact.

Japanese beetle was first detected at V13-V16 (0.8% detections in the field), not detected by the final mission, and was outside the pollination window. Stink bug was detected at R2-R4 (0.4%) and remained present at the final mission, with feeding within the kernel set window. European corn borer was detected during the season but not at the final mission, with whorl feeding at V6–V8. result_text:
Consider redesigning the weed management program with a stronger pre-emergence residual targeting pigweeds, barnyard grass, and broadleaf species to close the gap that allowed early-season escapes.

Be ready to spray a fungicide targeting Gray Leaf Spot, Northern Corn Leaf Blight, and Rust at the VT window if in-field and regional foliar disease pressure are similar to this season. Crop rotation and debris management reduce the risk of Gray Leaf Spot and Northern Corn Leaf Blight next year by minimizing overwintering fungus.

Review nutrient timing, placement, and loss mitigation practices. Consider soil sampling the affected areas and adjusting the fertility program before planting to address persistent potassium deficiency.

Consider a targeted response to stink bug at the R1–R3 window next season if pressure develops — monitor for stink bug presence beginning at early reproductive stages.
